answer: Each identity has one sable forge cast one piece from a fresh umber mould and locks a 70-credit bond, then files the broken fragments and piece serial on the mould ledger. The forge charges 34 credits for the first mould; the k-th mould costs 34+9(k-1), so the 1000th costs 9025 and 1000 fakes pay 4,529,500 plus 70,000 locked. An auditor fits fragments to the piece and burns the bond when fragments, serial, and ledger disagree. A mould-rental ring fails because broken fragments fit one cast, never a second. An honest smith pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
